source.title: Cameroon attacking corners: near-post overload vs Switzerland, clip 2

situation.outcome: The outswinging delivery is off target and cleared by the second zonal defender
situation.human_observation: Cameroon moved two players out of the penalty area to take the corner, with the stated aim of drawing the Swiss defenders out of position. Compared to clip 1's four front-post runners, this time Cameroon sent three runners towards the front post, with two further players making runs to the back post and the penalty spot respectively. The out-swinging delivery, however, was off target on this occasion, and the ball was cleared by the second zonal defender.
situation.priority_problem: How having two players positioned outside the box to take the corner (rather than solely inside) affects the opposition's defensive setup, and whether the front-post overload (three runners) and deeper runs (back post, penalty spot) can be converted if the delivery quality is not precise enough.
visible_evidence: Two Cameroon players move out of the penalty area to take the corner.
This positioning is intended to draw Swiss defenders out of position.
Three Cameroon runners attack the front-post area (fewer than the four used in clip 1).
Two further players make runs to the back post and the penalty spot respectively.
The delivery is out-swinging in flight.
The delivery is off target and is cleared by the second zonal defender before reaching any Cameroon attacker.

coaching.objective: Use a two-player short-corner setup to draw defenders out of position, while still committing runners to overload the front post and cover the back post/penalty-spot zones — and ensure delivery quality matches the movement so the overload can actually be exploited.
coaching.practice_design: Small-sided corner rehearsal where two attackers start outside the box specifically to draw defenders out before the corner is taken (rather than delivering directly from a single corner-taker). Three attackers time runs to the front post, one targets the back post, and one targets the penalty spot. Dedicate reps specifically to out-swinging delivery technique and consistency, since this clip's breakdown was a delivery/execution failure rather than a structural one — emphasise it must consistently beat the first defender and reach the front-post runners rather than drift off target.
success_cues: Two players positioned outside the box visibly draw at least one defender out of the central defensive shape before the corner is taken.
Three front-post runners arrive with correct timing relative to the delivery.
Back-post and penalty-spot runners hold their zones to offer a second/third option.
Delivery is out-swinging but on target, reaching the front-post zone rather than being cut out by the second zonal defender.
If delivery is off, review specifically whether it was a technical/execution issue (as in this instance) versus a structural/movement issue.

limitations: The brief clip may not show the complete pre-corner organisation.
